items.title: Russian hackers ran a cyberattack with AI and no human intervention
items.originalTitle: 2026. 11. 19. Emberi beavatkozás nélkül hajtottak végre kibertámadást mesterséges intelligenciával az orosz hackerek A Google Threat Intelligence Group és a Mandiant szakemberei szerint orosz nyelvű…
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report Russian-speaking actors executing an AI-driven attack without human operators in the loop, signalling growing autonomy in offensive tooling.

items.title: Java4Shell: attacker can achieve code execution without an account
items.originalTitle: 2026. 11. 19. Java4Shell: fiók nélkül is kódfuttatást érhet el a támadó Az Oracle novemberi Critical Security Patch Update csomagja 11 Java SE sérülékenységet javít. Ezek egyike a Java4Shell néven is…
items.summary: Oracle's November Critical Patch Update fixes 11 Java SE flaws, including one dubbed Java4Shell that can allow unauthenticated code execution. Patch internet-facing Java workloads first.

items.title: 2026-022: Critical vulnerabilities in Nginx
items.summary: F5 disclosed five NGINX vulnerabilities allowing unauthenticated remote code execution as the worker process; a PoC exists for CVE-2026-123007 but no in-the-wild exploitation yet. Patch internet-facing instances urgently.

items.title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
items.summary: Broadcom patched a critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass that Chinese-linked actors have exploited as a zero-day since September 2026. Immediate patching of vCenter is advised.

items.title: CVE-2026-123890: Critical Authentication Bypass in VMware vCenter
items.summary: Rapid7 details CVE-2026-123890, a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service of vCenter allowing unauthenticated attackers to gain Administrator access. Patch per VMSA-2026-0009.

items.title: Second Norwegian Energy Company Breached in Two Days
items.summary: A second Norwegian energy company was breached within two days; no formal link has been established between the incidents.

items.title: 6.4 million victim datasets secured in international operation against malware networks
items.summary: Europol and partners seized 235 servers and 257 domains used by Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC, securing 6.4 million victim datasets and disrupting major malware distribution networks.

items.title: 2026-021: High Severity Vulnerability in Java SE and OpenJDK
items.summary: CERT-EU advises patching CVE-2026-114938 in Java SE and OpenJDK, a high-severity flaw that can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions.

items.title: 2026-020: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
items.summary: Citrix fixed 28 memory flaws in NetScaler ADC and Gateway; CVE-2026-120868 affects all deployments including default configurations, with DoS and unpredictable behaviour impact. No exploitation reported.

items.title: Your AI red team may be finding the same prompt injection thousands of times
items.summary: Academic research found that AI agents retrained on larger sets of prompt injection attacks became easier to hijack in three of four tests, questioning volume-driven automated red teaming.

items.title: AI agent API security hasn’t caught up with agents already running in production
items.summary: A Postman survey of ~9,000 practitioners found a quarter of organisations already run AI agents calling production APIs, while around four in ten have not settled agent credential and identity management.

items.title: Most CIOs and CISOs expect to contain attacks, though few can reach their gear right away
items.summary: An Opengear survey of 514 CIOs and CISOs found few can obtain secure management access to critical network infrastructure immediately when the primary network fails, a key gap during ransomware or bad-update events.

items.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
items.summary: Round-up of critical VMware and KVM virtualization flaws arriving alongside Java and PHP patch waves, plus a notable Digital Ocean response to a nested virtualization issue.

items.title: Android developer verification will reach every install source, with a side door for power users
items.summary: From January 2027 Google extends Android developer verification worldwide across all install sources, starting with seven app distributors; unverified developers' apps lose the normal install experience.

items.title: Qwen Incidents Show Self-Hosted AI Models Need Stronger Steering
items.summary: Incidents involving Qwen models show that organisations self-hosting AI agents have only an illusion of control and need enforceable steering and guardrails.

items.title: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
items.summary: ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 fixing three critical flaws, including a hard-coded key, that could give remote attackers administrative control of the console and managed devices.

items.title: Chase, Visa, Mastercard confirm third-party cyberattacks that may have exposed customers' info
items.summary: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirmed cyberattacks on third-party vendors that may have exposed customer information, following a week of service outages.

items.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard say third-party vendors targeted in cyberattack
items.summary: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard say third-party vendors were targeted in a cyberattack, highlighting financial sector supply-chain exposure.

items.title: Critical PHP Flaws Allow Code Execution, But Don't Panic 'PHP2Shell'-Style
items.summary: PHP's November release patches seven critical flaws enabling code execution, though experts say exploitability depends heavily on configuration. Less severe than the earlier PHP2Shell issue.

items.title: The web is held together by volunteers. AI could tear it apart.
items.summary: Report on volunteer maintainers of core web infrastructure struggling to keep up as AI-driven analysis surfaces deeply hidden vulnerabilities.

items.title: Daily summary - 19.11.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report notes NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims and a further PHP Foundation warning on critical PHP vulnerabilities after PHP2Shell.

items.title: Critical security vulnerabilities in PHP - updates available
items.originalTitle: Kritische Sicherheitslücken in PHP - Updates verfügbar
items.summary: CERT.at reports PHP security updates fixing seven critical flaws in ext-session, ext-date, PHP-FPM and the Zend Engine that can lead to arbitrary code execution in certain configurations.

items.title: Spying on Governments with Zero Lines of Malware: A Custom SoftEther Bridge in Webworm’s Toolkit
items.summary: Rapid7 analyses a custom SoftEther VPN bridge used by China-aligned APT Webworm to maintain stealthy, malware-free long-term access to government networks.

items.title: EU, US officials unmoved by litigation potentially impacting Data Privacy Framework
items.summary: EU and US officials say they are not worried by ongoing litigation that could affect the Data Privacy Framework, maintaining confidence in the transatlantic transfer mechanism.

items.title: One year on, Digital Omnibus may face delays
items.summary: The EU's Digital Omnibus simplification package may be delayed a year after its launch, prolonging uncertainty for compliance planning.

items.title: Fraud data sharing under the new PSR: When a DPIA becomes the ticket of entry
items.summary: Analysis of fraud data sharing under the new Payment Services Regulation, where a data protection impact assessment becomes a precondition for participation.

items.title: 354 dark web vendors and buyers arrested in Europol-coordinated global crackdown
items.summary: Operation TorNado, coordinated by Europol across 14 countries, led to 354 arrests of dark web vendors and buyers tied to cybercrime, drugs and firearms between May 2025 and October 2026.

items.title: It’s time to retire vanity security dashboards
items.summary: An OT security architect argues for retiring vanity dashboards and instead having SOC and control engineering teams jointly tune recurring, low-value alerts.

items.title: Trump bows to pressure, replaces US cyber security director

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Taiwan tells Meta thousands of China-linked accounts seek to influence elections
items.summary: Taiwan has told Meta that thousands of China-linked accounts are seeking to influence its elections, according to a Reuters exclusive.

items.title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
items.summary: An unpatched Windows technique called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access to a locked PC launch programs without signing in, under a limited account rather than administrator.

items.title: White House replaces cyber security chief after tech outages
items.summary: Sean Cairncross leaves the US national cyber director role after a week of major tech outages; Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies takes over in an acting capacity.

items.title: Stockpiling Britain: Does Westminster know something we don’t?
items.summary: The UK government's 'Be Ready' campaign urges citizens to stockpile essentials, with planners citing 'Black Sky' scenarios such as a major blackout disrupting communications and supply chains.

items.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
items.summary: The founder of AI product ChatPRD describes large-scale token fraud, where groups abuse free trials to obtain or resell AI compute for commercial schemes.

items.title: Sean Cairncross out as national cyber director
items.summary: Sean Cairncross departs as US national cyber director after involvement in key decisions on AI security and critical infrastructure protection.

items.title: White House fires cyber director in wake of outages, sources say
items.summary: Sources say the White House fired the national cyber director following outages; the Pentagon CIO takes over while doubts grow about the CISA nominee.

items.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
items.summary: European leaders meeting in Berlin say they hold a united position and are ready for talks with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Medical Group customers
items.summary: SBC Medical Group disclosed in an SEC filing that two cybersecurity incidents exposed personal data of 1.6 million customers and employees.

items.title: Lawmakers launch new AI safety caucus amid rising security concerns
items.summary: US lawmakers launched a bipartisan AI safety caucus with 26 founding members, including seven Republicans, amid rising security concerns.

items.title: A cyberattack leaks thousands of Chase customer emails and some phone numbers
items.summary: A cyberattack leaked thousands of Chase customer email addresses and some phone numbers.

items.title: Costa eyes tax on Big Tech to boost EU budget after Trump’s poor midterms showing
items.summary: European Council President Costa is considering a tax on Big Tech to strengthen the EU budget, seeing an opening after Trump's midterm losses.

items.summary: Google built a large simulated 'mirror' internet as a sandbox to train and test Chrome AI browsing agents without real-world risk.

items.title: US maritime agency warned Iran blockade was adding to rising Gulf premiums
items.summary: A US Maritime Administration memo acknowledges that a naval blockade of Iran is pushing up Gulf insurance premiums and squeezing cargo capacity.

items.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner says President Trump is open to NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine.

items.summary: The White House appointed Kirsten Davies as acting national cyber director following a week of outages affecting US users.

items.summary: Anthropic surged in its market debut after the largest IPO on record, despite concerns about unchecked AI growth.

items.title: What’s With All These Outages?
items.summary: Podcast discussion of the week's widespread digital outages, Anthropic's IPO proceeds and the AI chip landscape.

items.summary: PostgreSQL 19 shipped two months late, partly due to a wave of AI-reported vulnerabilities the team had to triage; new features include WAIT FOR LSN read-your-writes consistency.

items.title: Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Highlights the AI Giant’s Worst Enemy—Itself
items.summary: Analysis of Anthropic's $107 billion IPO and whether its AI safety strategy and public backlash against data centres could constrain growth.

items.title: Missing authentication in Bazarr Plex OAuth API
items.summary: Bazarr before 1.5.7-beta.14 does not require API-key authentication for Plex OAuth API handlers. A network-reachable attacker can change persistent Plex configuration, disable or rebind the Plex integration, and potentially influence later server-side requests; some actions require no Plex account, PIN, or prior acces…

items.title: Route normalization access-control bypass in fabio
items.summary: Fabio versions before 1.7.3 can apply route ACL or basic-auth checks to a different path interpretation than the backend uses. An unauthenticated attacker may reach protected backend content when a less-restricted fallback route targets the same backend and that backend normalizes the requested path differently.
items.mitigation: Upgrade fabio to version 1.7.3 or later. Until upgraded, remove or restrict fallback routes that share backends with protected routes.

items.title: Authentication bypass via default JWT secret in sprout-track
items.summary: sprout-track versions before 1.3.5 may use a publicly known JWT signing secret when JWT_SECRET is not configured. An unauthenticated attacker able to reach the deployment could forge privileged authentication tokens and access or alter application data; deployments with a strong unique JWT_SECRET are not affected.
items.mitigation: Upgrade sprout-track to version 1.3.5. Set JWT_SECRET to a strong, unique value and restrict network access to the application until the upgrade is complete.
